clue.text: Blooming repeatedly further down

parts.note: inf. abbreviates Latin infra, below or further down, used in footnotes
lower means further down

explanation.surface: Something keeps flowering lower and lower down the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' tells you 'further down' is used twice: once as INF (infra, the reference abbreviation for 'below') and once as LOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that is blooming has its blossoms open, the idiom for which is being in bloom or in blossom.

clue.text: Non-striker embracing one who paints a beetle

indicators.note: embracing means the first word's synonym holds the second inside it

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike
RA, a Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A strike-breaker hugs an artist who is painting a beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle sacred in ancient Egypt, an example of the insect.

clue.text: Religious reformer dropped her in dry 12

indicators.note: in means the shortened name goes inside the word for dry

parts.note: to parch is to dry out

indicators.note: dropped means the word her is lost from the reformer's name

parts.note: Martin Luther led the Protestant Reformation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Protestant reformer, minus a woman, sits inside a dry biography.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch wrote the Parallel Lives of Greeks and Romans, so he is a classic writer of lives, the 12 answer.

clue.text: See 16
Death scene, extremely pleasant — rail off

indicators.note: off means the letters for rail come away from the phrase

parts.note: very nice means extremely pleasant
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A deathbed scene is very pleasant, except the railing is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Mann's novella is Death in Venice, so the city is where the death takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: Death in Venice sets its story in the Italian city, so the place is the scene of that death.

clue.text: gives the V and A a Hindu garment

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'gives the V and A a Hindu garment': the definition (presumably a cross-reference to 12, Vasari being a biographer) is missing from the start of the clue; wordplay is V + A + SARI.
annotationWithheld.clue: gives the V and A a Hindu garment

clue.text: In league with a pupil, was a romancer

parts.note: L is a learner, a pupil driver
to romance can mean to tell fanciful stories, so a romancer lied

explanation.surface: Someone teamed up with a student and spun romantic fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allied means joined in alliance, a synonym for being in league with someone.

clue.text: Cleaned, when all's done?

definitions.meaning: a task done and ... is completely finished

explanation.definitionFit: Dusted means wiped clean, and the idiom done and dusted means fully finished.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about cleaner work with inability to bear

parts.note: into means keen on, as in being into jazz

indicators.note: work means the letters of cleaner are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a cleaner's work cannot stand much else.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerance is being unable to put up with something, a synonym of inability to bear it.

clue.text: Home Guard pursuing wood and stone

parts.note: ash is a timber tree
a Lar was a Roman household god guarding the home

explanation.surface: Home Guard volunteers chase after timber and rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' signals the order: the guard comes after the wood. 'Home Guard' looks like Britain's wartime volunteer militia, but here it is a Roman household god.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is squared, dressed building stone, a specific kind of stone.

clue.text: Time after crazy nut with 5 down's garment I would remove

indicators.note: after means the T for time comes at the end
crazy means the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the Hindu garment in 5 down's clue is the sari

explanation.surface: Time follows a crazy fellow wearing a sari he plans to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' scrambles the nut and the sari together, and 'after' puts Time at the end. The definition is what a nudist might say about any garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who would take off their clothes on principle is a nudist, which the answer means.

clue.text: Defensive measure ensuring game finished level?

parts.note: a game finished level is a draw
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A tactic guarantees that a match ends in a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: the second piece is the game, the first how it finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge, raised over a moat, is a castle's defence, a fair example of a defensive measure.

clue.text: Boswell's first … with hero a prig? Hardly!

definitions.text: Boswell's first … with hero a prig? Hardly!

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of Boswell's
hardly here signals the words are rearranged, the hero being anything but a prig

explanation.surface: Boswell's subject, Dr Johnson, was a hero to him and no prig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly!' rearranges the words after the B. James Boswell wrote the Life of Samuel Johnson, whom he admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Boswell is the model writer of another person's life, which is what the answer names.

clue.text: The right house to put in a family or similar group

indicators.note: to put in means the words go inside the family's synonym

parts.note: a brood is a family of young
taken as written

explanation.surface: The proper home to place a family, or some such group.
explanation.definitionFit: A brotherhood is a fraternity or society, a group bonded like a family.

clue.text: This is always happening to me: I'm my own 12 …

definitions.text: This is always happening to me
definitions.meaning: a resigned catchphrase for a familiar misfortune
a writer of their own life is an autobiographer, who tells their own tale

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a rueful idiom for recurring bad luck, and literally an autobiography's subject.

clue.text: See 14
… I expected a lot: page to call speaker with up and down epitaphs

parts.note: hi is a greeting call
the lip is the speaker's mouth; lip also means talk

indicators.note: up and down means the name reads the same both ways

parts.note: Pip took his surname from the epitaphs on his parents' tombstones

explanation.surface: A page boy summons a speaker carrying epitaphs from above and below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I expected a lot' points at Pip, hero of Dickens's Great Expectations; his surname, from the tombstones, is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Pip narrates Great Expectations, so he is the person who expected a lot.

clue.text: See 11
Leader of group to price manual?

parts.note: a charge is a price
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A team leader puts a price on a handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargehand is a foreman in charge of a small team of workers, a group leader.

clue.text: Far from meteor?

indicators.note: from means the answer is made out of the letters of meteor

explanation.surface: A long way off from a shooting star.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means distant, a straightforward synonym of far.

clue.text: Mother and child in a jam?

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A mother and her child find themselves in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsons are plums often made into preserves, so one is found in a jam.

clue.text: Sea horse

definitions.meaning: Latin for sea, used for the lunar seas

explanation.definitionFit: Mare names a lunar sea plain and also a female horse.

clue.text: Go up to the top of the house, say, with such change coming

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken to give the answer's sound

parts.words: Go up to the top of the house
parts.note: climb attic, ascending to the room under the roof

explanation.surface: Climbing to the attic while a big change is on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Climatic change is change in the climate, so the adjective describes that coming change.

clue.text: Mother a gentlewoman? There'll be trouble

parts.note: ma is mother
a lady is a gentlewoman

explanation.surface: Mother is a refined lady, which will mean trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or ailment, a kind of trouble with health.

clue.text: Hoist used in heist?

parts.note: an explosive charge for blowing doors, in Hamlet's 'hoist with his own' phrase

explanation.definitionFit: A petard is a small bomb for breaching gates, the device in the idiom hoist with one's own.

clue.text: Contemptuous expression uttered by Humpty

indicators.note: uttered means the exclamation is spoken aloud

parts.note: pouf is an exclamation of contempt

explanation.surface: Humpty Dumpty utters a scornful remark.
explanation.walkthrough: A humpty is a British name for a low padded seat; the surface pulls towards Humpty Dumpty.
explanation.definitionFit: A humpty is a solid cushion seat, another name for a footstool of that kind.
